arguments.prompt: Locked-off eye-height wide from the wet paving twenty-six metres out, looking straight at City Hall. The long timber stage crosses the lower third of the frame as one horizontal band, parallel to the building, finishing at a tall garlanded pine upright in the right-hand quarter with open wet granite beyond it. The camera is locked off on a tripod and does not move at all: no pan, no tilt, no zoom, no drift, no handheld shake. Real-time speed, natural human movement, never slow motion. A workman in a high-visibility vest and white hard hat, in profile at the short flight of steps against the stage front, puts his weight on the first tread, bounces once, nods, steps down and walks out of the frame to the right at an ordinary pace. Everything else holds still: the single line of folding chairs stays a single line, the podium, the crossbeam, the pumpkins and hay bales along the stage front, the corn sheaves at the columns and the banner. A heavy flat overcast, sheet-cake grey sky, no sun and no shadows; a light steady drizzle falls, fine rain visible against the dark stone, the granite paving wet with shallow puddles mirroring the grey sky; street lamps and windows glow warm and are doubled in the wet. On the far street beyond the square and along the side kerbs a few cars move slowly and steadily with their headlights and tail-lights on, reflected in the wet road, at an unhurried city pace - no car ever enters the square or comes near the stage. Prestige political drama photographed on an Arri Alexa with anamorphic lenses: flat overcast daylight, slight 35mm film grain, colours desaturated about twelve percent, warm tungstens, deep browns and charcoals in the shadows, photographic realism.
